Subject: ACME Logistics — technical recap & proposed PoC (latency / throughput)

Samira / Daniel — thanks again for taking the time today. Below is a concise recap of what we heard during the call, the technical constraints you called out, and the proposal for a short PoC to validate latency and throughput SLOs. Please flag anything I missed.

Quick recap of pain & goals
- Primary goal: integrate LLM-powered intent classification + short-form summarization into the dispatch UI with sub-300ms p95 inference and consistent throughput for peak routing windows.
- Pain points: current prototype spikes to 1s+ p95 at peak, unpredictable cold-starts, and concerns about data residency for PII in logs.
- Business impact sought: reduce operator handling time by 20% and speed up route assignment during peak by ~2x.

Model & workload assumptions (from call)
- Core model: customer prefers an open 13B-class decoder-only model (quantized) for cost/latency tradeoffs.
- Typical request shape: ~12–40 tokens generated (summaries), prompt prefix ~120 tokens (context + metadata).
- Expected traffic: 100 sustained RPS during normal hours; peaks to 350 RPS for short bursts (10–20s) during shift handoffs.

Latency / throughput SLOs (draft)
- Target: p95 <= 300ms for 40-token outputs (end-to-end generation latency) under 100 RPS sustained.
- Degraded mode: fall back to a smaller 7B variant for p95 <= 200ms when cost or capacity constraints hit; routed automatically.
- Throughput: support 350 RPS burst for 20s with autoscaling/fallback; predictable tail latencies required.

Deployment topology we recommend
- Private (VPC) Dedicated deployment in us-west-2 for primary traffic (data residency + audit controls).
- Reserved GPU pool sized for 100 RPS sustained on the 13B quantized variant, with burst capacity routed to hosted Redwood instances (same model family) for short peaks.
- KV/prefix caching for stable route prompts and a small cache TTL to reduce per-token compute on repeats.
- Observability: token-level cost/time breakdowns, per-request tracing, and model output regression alerts tied to your eval prompts.

Next steps / proposed PoC (2–4 weeks)
1) Exchange sample prompts and 500 representative calls (anonymized) — ACME to provide by 2026-03-18.
2) Redwood will provision a dedicated PoC pool and run a benchmark under your traffic profile (we'll focus on p50/p95/p99 and throughput).
3) Joint review of results + parameter tuning (quantization, batch sizing, autoscale policy).
4) Draft SLA and pricing for Dedicated capacity (attached).

Deliverables we will provide
- PoC runbook + test harness (attached).
- Benchmark report with latency/throughput curves and cost projection.
- Draft SLA and proposed committed capacity.

Open questions we flagged on the call
- Are logs going to include any customer PII we need to redact before sending to Redwood? (You mentioned token-level logs should be scrubbed.)
- Any compliance constraints beyond SOC2 / VPC isolation (e.g., industry-specific retention rules)?
- Expected timeline for procurement if PoC looks good.

If that aligns, I'll schedule the PoC kickoff with Connor and Marissa for next week. Suggested slots: Tue 2026-03-17 10:00–11:30 or Wed 2026-03-18 13:00–14:30 PT.

Thanks — Ben

Ben — thanks for the thorough recap. A couple quick clarifying questions before we share the test data:  
1) Can Redwood guarantee p95 <= 300ms at 100 RPS sustained for the 13B quantized model, or is that a best-effort target? We need an SLA floor for production.  
2) For the degraded mode (7B fallback), what’s the expected quality delta on the summarization task? Do you have a quick metric (e.g., accuracy/ROUGE delta) or will this be part of the PoC?

If you can sketch answers to those two we’ll prioritize sending a sanitized sample set.

—Daniel

d.price@acmelogistics.com

Subject: Re: ACME Logistics — technical recap & proposed PoC (latency / throughput)

Daniel — quick answers:  
1) SLA / guarantee: For production on Dedicated capacity we can contract an SLA around availability and Maximum Acceptable Latency tiers. Because latency depends on request shape and model variant, our standard approach is to commit to p95 <= 300ms for the agreed benchmark workload (the one we'll run during PoC). In short: not a blanket single-number guarantee without the benchmark — but we will bind the SLA to the validated PoC profile. I’ve attached the SLA draft for procurement review (redwood-sla-draft-v1.pdf).

2) 7B fallback quality: the exact delta depends on prompt engineering and the eval set. In prior customers’ benchmarks we typically see a modest drop in summary fidelity (human-evaluated quality delta ~5–12% depending on task), but for short extracts/intent classification the delta can be <5%. We'll quantify this during the PoC with your sanitized prompts and provide a side-by-side evaluation (ROUGE / human samples).

I'll also call out two ways we reduce tail latency: 1) short-lived warm pools + pre-warming for scheduled peaks, 2) prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts. Both will be part of the PoC tuning.

Next: we'll ingest the anonymized sample set and schedule the benchmark. I’ll send calendar invites after you confirm the kickoff slot.

Best — Ben
